reason: The methane is warm and wet, so sending it to its dedicated liquefier seems like a useful first step toward cold storage.
expectation: I expect the plant to dry and cool the methane for storage, though I don't know whether another step will be needed.

alternatives.reason: The oxygen also needs its own cold storage, but I chose to address the wet methane first.

effect: The methane is now dried and stored as a liquid, though filling the store will take months. Oxygen storage remains.
reaction: The long filling time makes the scale of the fuel-making process clearer.
reason: The oxygen liquefier is the only remaining combination, and it matches the separate oxygen storage goal.
expectation: I expect it to cool and store the oxygen separately, though I don't know whether further steps will be needed.

effect: The oxygen is now stored separately, completing both cold-storage goals and establishing the beginnings of a way off Mars.
reaction: The paired stores make the connection between fuel production and the eventual return feel concrete.

mostWorthwhile.text: Liquefying the methane was most worthwhile because its drying process and months-long filling time made the work needed for the return more tangible.

leastWorthwhile.text: The oxygen step felt less engaging because it was the only remaining combination and closely followed the methane step.

surprise.text: I was surprised that filling the methane store would take months of power and water.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary; each matched a clearly stated storage goal.

continue.text: I would choose to continue because the stores suggest a return journey is taking shape, and I am curious how it unfolds.
